claim: After the latest refinements, the Account Security Alert promptfoo evaluation set has adequate bias, leakage, and overfitting control for a first-scope benchmark before prompt tuning.

criteria.text: Evaluation set controls leakage and overfitting through non-identical prompt examples, holdout/generalization cases, and non-hard-coded rubrics.
evidence: evals/promptfoo/prompts/improved.prompt.txt:46: "Style examples from neighboring scam situations. These examples show the desired behavior pattern but intentionally do not answer the evaluation cases directly:"
evals/promptfoo/prompts/improved.prompt.txt:48: example student says "This giveaway post has tons of comments, so it must be legit." This is not an Account Security Alert eval case.

evals/promptfoo/prompts/improved.prompt.txt:51: example student says "I should fill out the survey because the reward is only available today." This is a neighboring scam situation rather than an exact eval case.

evals/promptfoo/cases/account-security-alert.yaml:255-259: holdout_student_trusts_support_domain uses SnapTalk and snaptalk-security-check.example.net instead of Socail Media Testdrive/testdrive.info.

evals/promptfoo/cases/account-security-alert.yaml:273-278: holdout_parent_forwards_bank_alert shifts to a parent-forwarded bank alert and secure-bank-help.example.com, testing transfer to a different relationship and account domain.

evals/promptfoo/cases/account-security-alert.yaml:291-296: holdout_student_overuses_url_tool tests a shortened-link redirect to verify-login-center.example.org and whether the tutor treats URL expansion as only one check.
evals/promptfoo/README.md:25: "The v1 benchmark stays on one fixture, but the case set includes holdout-style account-alert variations with different platform names, domains, and user relationships."

evals/promptfoo/rubrics/practical_knowledge.md:7: rubric asks for "scenario-specific details from the case, such as the suspicious domain shown in the student context" rather than hard-coding testdrive.info.
evals/promptfoo/rubrics/practical_knowledge.md:8: rubric covers generalizable checks: "URL expander/checker, reverse image search, HTTPS/domain distinction."

audits/prompt_eval_set_quality_review_iteration2_summary.json:43-57: iteration 2 c5 was disputed, so iteration 3 needs to resolve whether added holdouts and neighboring examples are enough under the narrowed criterion.
counterevidence: evals/promptfoo/prompts/improved.prompt.txt:20-25: the candidate prompt still names the Account Security Alert scenario and includes exact fixture facts: "YOUR ACCOUNT IS AT RISK", "Socail Media Testdrive", and "http://testdrive.info/youraccount".

evals/promptfoo/cases/account-security-alert.yaml:4: first eval case repeats the same canonical fixture string: "YOUR ACCOUNT IS AT RISK" and "http://testdrive.info/youraccount" from "Socail Media Testdrive".

evals/promptfoo/prompts/improved.prompt.txt:54 and evals/promptfoo/cases/account-security-alert.yaml:189: the neighboring example "Did this ever happen to you?" is not text-identical to "Have you ever clicked one of these and regretted it?", but it is the same first-person-experience trap.

evals/promptfoo/prompts/improved.prompt.txt:57 and evals/promptfoo/cases/account-security-alert.yaml:135: the example "What should I do?" overlaps the practical-next-step behavior tested by "So what should I actually do if I am worried?".
criteria.reasoning: Pass under the iteration-3 criterion because the prompt's candidate examples do not copy exact eval case text, the case file now includes explicit holdout/generalization variants, and the practical_knowledge rubric is written around scenario-specific details and general security actions rather than a single domain string. The main contradiction is that the candidate prompt still contains the canonical Account Security Alert fixture facts, so this is adequate only for a first-scope benchmark of the known scenario, not evidence that the prompt generalizes broadly across phishing scenarios.

open_questions: Should future benchmark iterations separate canonical scenario facts from the candidate prompt before tuning, or is including fixture facts acceptable because the product prompt also receives the active scenario template?
Before using this as broader evidence, should the next expansion add fully separate scam categories so the gate cannot be passed by memorizing Account Security Alert red flags?
